plan_title: Purdy-Bradley Springer Field: Northeast Purdy Springer Unit (NEPSU) / South East Bradley A Unit (SEBAU) Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The combined NEPSU and SEBAU unit boundaries plus a buffer of at least one-half mile, where the free-phase CO2 is expected to stay through 2054 and five years after (p34).
mma_definition: Defined as identical to the AMA: the two unit boundaries plus a half-mile buffer, since the plume is expected to be held by the reservoir's geologic truncation limits (p6, p34-35).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Wellbores (especially legacy wells and drilling of new wells) and surface equipment are treated as the realistic pathways ('unlikely but possible'); shallow groundwater wells, faults/fractures, lateral movement, the confining seal and seismicity are all rated unlikely with low magnitude (p5, p36-39, p41, p46).
baseline_summary: No pre-injection environmental baseline. The baseline is ongoing operational data on injection well pressures and rates plus pattern performance; the plan may elect to collect ambient air data later. Reference gas values cited: 0.6% CO2 in the Cunningham before 1982 injection, 0.25% average in Hart wells sampled October 2023, and basin-wide published CO2 ranges, to be consulted if a leak is detected (p39, p46).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with the mass balance (Equation RR-11) and any leakage events with estimated amounts; records kept at least three years; mechanical failures of surface casing or cement reported to the appropriate regulatory authority. No commitment to publish measurement data (p42, p45, p47, p50, p53).

rows.detail: Orifice meter with digital transducer and ROC800 flow computer on received CO2 pipeline; meters at Purdy Tee, plant outlet, recycle point and each injection well; composition sampled routinely, produced gas quarterly.
rows.location: Pipeline receipt point, Lindsay plant outlet, recycle compressor, each injection well
rows.evidence_quote: A flow meter at each injection well measures the injection rate of the CO2 or water.

rows.detail: Wellhead injection pressure monitored continually; injection rates reported daily and compared with pattern WAG targets; SCADA data warehouse; WAG skid pressures monitored continuously.
rows.location: Each CO2 injection well and WAG skids
rows.trigger_or_response: Statistically significant deviation from target rate/pressure or permit limits: screened and investigated; corrective plan if leakage indicated.
rows.evidence_quote: Well pressure in injection wells is monitored on a continual basis.

rows.detail: Casing (tubing-casing annulus) pressure monitored on each injection well as part of MIT program and to detect tubing leaks.
rows.trigger_or_response: Annulus pressure change indicating tubing leak: workover crews respond within days.
rows.evidence_quote: Injection pressures and casing pressures are monitored on each CO2 injection well.

rows.detail: MIT under OAC 165:10-5-6 using pressure recorder and annulus pressure test; initial MIT then at least every year or every five years depending on permitted injection rate.
rows.trigger_or_response: Loss of mechanical integrity: well immediately shut in, investigation initiated, leak documented and corrected.
rows.evidence_quote: subsequent MIT at least once every year or every 5 years, depending on the permitted injection rate

rows.detail: Each producer diverted to satellite test equipment about every 1-2 months (roughly 24 hours) to measure and sample fluids; produced gas sampled quarterly at plant; volumes compared with forecasts.
rows.location: Each production well via 10 satellite batteries; Lindsay plant inlet and tailgate
rows.trigger_or_response: Production off plan: engineering/operations investigate; leak documented, reported and corrected if found.
rows.evidence_quote: with each well being tested approximately once every 1-2 months

rows.detail: Reservoir pressure named as an example monitoring provision and for the end-of-period demonstration, but the plan admits no recent reservoir pressure measurements exist and names no gauges or observation wells.
rows.trigger_or_response: Seismicity creating a pathway would be flagged by reservoir pressure, well pressure and pattern monitoring, prompting investigation.
rows.evidence_quote: other reservoir fluid monitoring provisions (e.g., reservoir pressure, well pressure, and pattern monitoring) would lead to further investigation

rows.detail: Field personnel (about 20) inspect wells, facilities, pipelines and equipment weekly or daily, looking for CO2 clouds, frost, stains, dead animals, vegetation change and unapproved drilling.
rows.trigger_or_response: Visible vapor or ice: reported, documented, corrective plan; workover crews within days.
rows.evidence_quote: Daylight’s field personnel conduct routine weekly or daily inspections of the facilities, wells, and other equipment

rows.detail: No background soil gas collection; shallow vapor monitoring points, flux box or ring tent offered only as examples the operator may elect to use to verify and quantify a detected leak.
rows.trigger_or_response: Possible leakage event detected: may install vapor monitoring points or flux box to quantify.
rows.evidence_quote: Daylight may elect to use vapor monitoring points installed into the shallow subsurface as part of the leakage verification and quantification process.

rows.detail: One shallow groundwater well within the AMA to be tested annually; water samples also taken from shallow wells during Class II permit applications. Plan elsewhere says USDW wells have not been monitored.
rows.location: One groundwater well within the AMA (about 85 shallow wells exist)
rows.trigger_or_response: Any reported groundwater change: investigated to eliminate the potential leakage pathway.
rows.evidence_quote: Daylight will test a groundwater well within the AMA on an annual basis to provide additional monitoring for potential leakage.

rows.detail: One-time October 2023 gas sampling of more than 50 wells producing from the overlying Hart Sandstone (0.25% CO2) used to show the seal holds; no ongoing above-zone program.
rows.trigger_or_response: Values to be consulted as reference if a potential leak is detected.
rows.evidence_quote: Daylight’s testing of more than 50 wells producing from the Hart reservoir showed an average of 0.25% molar concentration of CO2

rows.detail: Radioactive tracer survey run in some instances, in addition to or instead of MIT, when required by permit or regulator to confirm fluids enter the injection zone.
rows.trigger_or_response: If investigation identifies a leak: shut in, document, report, corrective plan.
rows.evidence_quote: Daylight is required to perform a RTS to ensure that all injection fluids are going into the injection zone.

rows.detail: One-time review of the USGS earthquake catalog (M2.5+ within 2 miles of the MMA, accessed January 2025); no site seismometers and no commitment to ongoing network monitoring.
rows.trigger_or_response: Response plan: shut in injectors near a seismic event, detected via WAG skid pressure monitoring.
rows.evidence_quote: data obtained from the United States Geological Survey [USGS] Earthquakes Hazard Program catalog

rows.detail: Operator may elect to collect ambient air detector data to characterize baseline values; no commitment.
rows.evidence_quote: Daylight may elect to collect additional atmospheric test data using ambient air detectors or other methodologies to characterize baseline values in the units.

rows.detail: Continuous rate and pressure monitoring of the CO2 pipeline and the capture/compression/dehydration facility with high and low set-point alarms to operators.
rows.trigger_or_response: Parameter outside allowable window: operators alerted; delivery-point-only flags sent to field staff to investigate for leak.
rows.evidence_quote: monitors the rates and pressures at the facility and on the pipeline on a continuous basis.

rows.detail: Subpart W emission factors (Table W-1A) for equipment leaks and vents between meters and wellheads; engineering estimates or modeling for event-driven surface leaks.
rows.evidence_quote: Daylight will use Subpart W techniques to estimate leakages only on equipment

rows.detail: Wellhead pressure of temporarily abandoned (inactive) wells, isolated with bridge plugs, checked on an operations schedule for changes.
rows.evidence_quote: The wellhead pressures are then checked per operation schedule for any change.

notes: Figure pages (p10-12, 14-15, 17-19, 23-25, 27-29, 32-33, 37, 40) carry only captions; Figure 22 well map and the Appendix 1 well list (886 wellbores) are not in the text. Groundwater is contradictory: p36 commits to annual testing of one groundwater well, while p46 says USDW wells have not been monitored; coded as committed on the explicit 'will test' sentence. MIT frequency is annual or five-yearly depending on permitted rate, so coded multi_year. Reservoir pressure is listed as a monitoring provision, yet p30 says actual reservoir pressure was unavailable and the last measurement dates to Fox et al. (1988); hence mentioned_only. Visual inspection frequency is stated as 'weekly or daily' (p42), daily for surface equipment (p46), weekly in Table 4; coded weekly as the floor. Soil gas and RTS use permissive 'may elect'/'sometimes' language. No fresh CO2 has been received since 2022; implementation is expected in 2026 after approval and securing a new CO2 supply (p13, p50). No seismic surveys, personal or fixed gas detectors, InSAR or microseismic arrays are mentioned.
